To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

intratumoral injection is a feasible and safe method for delivering DCs to patients with advanced solid tumors and that combination of DCs with other immunotherapeutic agents may be a viable strategy to enhance clinical efficacy.
intratumoral injection is a safe, effective, and feasible method of delivering autologous activated T cells and DCs in combination with conventional therapies to cancer patients with advanced tumors.
direct intratumoral administration of DCs is safe and effective, with clinical responses in patients with advanced cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of autologous dendritic cells to induce antitumor immunity in patients with advanced cancers.
the use of dendritic cells (DC) in cancer immunotherapy.
the development of new cancer therapies that combine conventional treatments with immunotherapeutic strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DC‐based therapy is safe and feasible in patients with cancer, and that combination strategies are likely to be more effective than monotherapy.
DCs are a promising tool in the treatment of cancer, but the clinical results are disappointing.
DCs are not the most effective antigen-presenting cells for the induction of tumor-specific immune responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of conventional therapies (chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and surgery) with intratumoral injection with activated T cells and DCs is safe and effective for the treatment of patients with advanced cancer.
the use of DCs in combination with other conventional therapies may be an effective strategy for the treatment of advanced cancers.
the combination of conventional therapies with intratumoral injection is well tolerated and may be a useful strategy to enhance antitumor immunity in patients with advanced cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of DCs and activated T cells with chemotherapy and radiotherapy is a safe and effective strategy for treating patients with advanced solid tumors.
intratumoral injection with DCs and T cells is safe and can induce clinical responses, even in patients with advanced disease.
intratumoral injection with autologous DCs and activated T cells can be safely used as an adjuvant therapy to treat cancer patients.
